academy.tagged_body:
Why Is It So Hard to Put Down Your Phone?

{{g:Have you ever picked up|현재완료 경험: Have you ever + p.p.? (~해 본 적 있니?)}} your phone to check one message and {{g:found yourself still scrolling|find + 목적어 + -ing: ~가 …하고 있는 것을 발견하다}} thirty minutes later? You are not alone. Many teenagers {{g:find it difficult to stop|가목적어 it + 진목적어 to부정사}} using their phones, and {{t:there is a scientific reason for this}}.

When we get a "like" or a new message, our brain {{v:releases}} a {{v:chemical}} {{g:called dopamine|과거분사구(called ~)가 명사를 뒤에서 꾸밈: ~라고 불리는}}. Dopamine {{g:makes us feel good|사역동사 make + 목적어 + 동사원형}}, so our brain wants to repeat the experience again and again. App designers know this very well. That is why many apps use {{v:features}} such as {{v:endless}} scrolling and red {{v:notification}} dots, {{g:which are designed to keep|계속적 용법 관계대명사 which(= and they) + 수동태 be designed to: ~하도록 만들어지다}} us looking at the screen.

Using a phone too much can cause several problems. It can make it harder to fall asleep, {{v:reduce}} our ability to {{v:focus}}, and even make us feel more {{v:anxious}}.

{{v:Fortunately}}, there are simple ways to take back control. {{g:Try turning off|try + -ing: 시험 삼아 ~해 보다}} notifications for apps you don't need. Keep your phone outside your bedroom at night. You can also set a {{v:daily}} time limit in your phone's settings. {{t:Your phone should be a useful tool, not something that controls your life.}}

advanced.tagged_body:
Why Is It So Hard to Put Down Your Phone?

Have you ever picked up your phone just to check a single message, {{g:only to find yourself still scrolling|only to + 동사원형: (그런데) 결국 ~하게 되다 (뜻밖의 결과)}} thirty minutes later? If so, you are far from alone. A great number of teenagers {{v:struggle}} to stop using their phones, and {{t:science can explain why this happens}}.

Whenever we receive a "like" or a new message, our brain {{v:releases}} a chemical known as dopamine. Because dopamine produces a {{v:pleasant}} feeling, our brain is {{v:motivated}} to repeat the experience over and over. App designers are well {{v:aware}} of this. {{g:This is precisely why|This is why + 주어 + 동사: 그것이 바로 ~하는 이유이다}} so many apps include features like endless scrolling and red notification dots, {{g:both of which|수량 표현 + 관계대명사: both of which = and both of them}} are designed to keep our eyes fixed on the screen.

{{v:Excessive}} phone use can lead to a number of problems. It can make it more difficult to fall asleep, {{v:weaken}} our ability to {{v:concentrate}}, and even increase our feelings of anxiety.

Fortunately, there are several simple {{v:strategies}} for {{v:regaining}} control. {{g:Consider turning off|consider + -ing: ~하는 것을 고려하다}} notifications for apps that you do not really need. Leave your phone outside your bedroom at night. In addition, you can set a daily time limit in your phone's settings. {{t:After all, your phone should serve as a useful tool}} {{g:rather than|A rather than B: B라기보다는 A}} something that controls your life.

prestudy.tagged_body:
Why Is It So Hard to Put Down Your Phone?

Have you ever reached for your phone intending merely to check a single message, {{g:only to discover|only to + 동사원형: (그런데) 결국 ~하게 되다 (뜻밖의 결과)}} that you were still scrolling half an hour later? If so, you are by no means alone. A considerable number of {{v:adolescents}} find it remarkably difficult to {{v:disengage}} from their phones, and {{t:there is a well-established scientific explanation for this phenomenon}}.

{{g:Each time we receive|Each time + 주어 + 동사: ~할 때마다 (접속사 역할)}} a "like" or a new message, our brain releases a {{v:neurotransmitter}} called dopamine. Since dopamine generates a sense of pleasure, the brain is driven to seek out the same experience repeatedly. App developers are acutely aware of this {{v:mechanism}}. {{g:It is precisely for this reason that|It is ~ that 강조구문: 바로 ~ 때문에 …하다}} numerous applications {{v:incorporate}} features such as infinite scrolling and red notification badges, {{g:all of which|수량 표현 + 관계대명사: all of which = and all of them}} are {{v:deliberately}} engineered to keep users' attention fixed on the screen.

Excessive smartphone use can give rise to a variety of problems. {{g:Not only can it make|부정어 Not only가 문장 앞 → 조동사 + 주어 도치}} it harder to fall asleep, but it can also {{v:impair}} our capacity to concentrate and even {{v:heighten}} feelings of anxiety.

Fortunately, there are straightforward strategies for regaining control. Consider disabling notifications for {{v:nonessential}} applications. {{g:Make it a habit to leave|make it a habit to + 동사원형: ~하는 것을 습관으로 삼다 (가목적어 it)}} your phone outside your bedroom at night. Additionally, you can establish a daily usage limit in your phone's settings. {{t:Ultimately, your phone ought to remain a useful tool rather than something that}} {{v:dictates}} how you live.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of the passage?
choices: To argue that smartphones should be banned for adolescents
To praise app developers for their creative designs
To describe the history of the smartphone industry
To compare the effects of dopamine on adults and children
To explain the neurological and design-related causes of compulsive phone use and offer practical remedies
questions.answer: To explain the neurological and design-related causes of compulsive phone use and offer practical remedies
questions.explanation: 뇌 화학(도파민)과 앱 디자인이라는 원인을 설명하고, 실천 가능한 해결책을 제시하는 글이다.

items: Overuse undermines sleep, focus, and emotional well-being.

answer: A common experience reveals how difficult it is to disengage from phones.

essays.q: Explain in 2–3 English sentences why app developers can be said to "exploit" the brain's reward system.
essays.sampleAnswer: App developers know that dopamine creates pleasure and makes the brain seek the same experience again. They deliberately add features like infinite scrolling and red badges to trigger this response. In this way, they use the brain's reward system to keep users on the screen.
essays.rubric: ① 도파민 보상 원리 이해 ② 의도적 기능 설계(무한 스크롤·빨간 배지) ③ 화면에 붙잡아 두는 결과 ④ 영어 문장 2~3개, 문법 오류 없음

essays.sampleAnswer: 문제: ① 잠들기 어려워진다. ② 집중력이 손상된다. ③ 불안감이 커진다. 어순: 부정어 Not only가 문장 앞에 나와서 조동사 can과 주어 it의 순서가 바뀌었다(도치).

essays.q: 다음 우리말을 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오. '우리가 휴대폰을 내려놓기 어려운 것은 바로 도파민 때문이다.' <조건> It is ~ that 강조구문을 사용할 것 / find it hard to를 사용할 것

essays.rubric: ① It is because of dopamine that 강조구문 ② find it hard to + 동사원형 ③ put down our phones ④ 의미 일치

essays.q: 우리말로 쓰시오: 글쓴이가 제시한 세 가지 해결책이 각각 본문의 어떤 원인이나 문제를 줄이는 데 도움이 되는지 연결하여 설명하시오.
essays.sampleAnswer: ① 불필요한 앱의 알림을 끄면 빨간 알림 배지 같은 자극이 줄어 도파민을 좇아 휴대폰을 확인하는 일이 줄어든다. ② 밤에 휴대폰을 침실 밖에 두면 잠들기 어려운 문제를 줄일 수 있다. ③ 하루 사용 시간을 제한하면 과다 사용 자체가 줄어 집중력 저하와 불안을 막는 데 도움이 된다.
essays.rubric: 해결책 3가지를 각각 본문의 원인·문제와 논리적으로 연결하면 만점, 2가지면 부분 점수

essays.q: Summarize the passage in about 40 English words. Include the cause, the problems, and the solutions.
essays.sampleAnswer: Phones are hard to put down because dopamine makes us seek pleasure and apps are designed to exploit this. Overuse can harm sleep, focus, and emotions, but disabling notifications, keeping phones out of bedrooms, and setting time limits can help.
essays.rubric: ① 원인(도파민 + 앱 설계) ② 문제(수면·집중·불안) ③ 해결책(3가지 중 2가지 이상) ④ 40단어 내외
